newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's SEC says no conspiracy to defraud.
newsitem.headline: Manila's SEC says no conspiracy to defraud.

text.p: Philippine Securities and Exchange Commission chairman Perfecto Yasay said on Monday an initial investigation of four brokerages revealed that there was no conspiracy to defraud a well-known newspaper columnist.
Columnist Ninez Cacho-Olivares accused her broker, Jose Maximo Cuaycong, of using the four firms to make unauthorised transactions on her account.
"The findings seem to indicate that they were not conspirators with Cuaycong but their violations were more in the nature of failure to supervise their agents," Yasay told reporters.
Cuaycong was a trader of Abacus Securities Corp, and later of Dharmala Securities. Cacho-Olivares said Cuaycong also held accounts in Lippo Securities and Sapphire Securities.
However, Yasay said the SEC brokers and exchange department, which audited the four brokerage firms, had found violations of the Revised Securities Act in handling the Cacho-Olivares accounts.
The violations included allowing unlicenced traders to handle accounts, not time-stamping order tickets, short-selling, managing the account without the approval of the special power of attorney.
Yasay said a public hearing has been set within the next two weeks for the four houses to explain why they should not be penalised for violating some provisions of the Revised Securities Act.
But if imposed, these would only be light administration sanctions, he added.

"The interest of the SEC here is to make sure that the rules are followed. We do not intend to come up with severe penalties like revocation of licenses. In fact, we want the brokerage firms to help us come up with a system to ensure that something like this will not happen again," Yasay said.
Lippo Securities and Abacus Securities, in separate letters to the SEC, denied some of the alleged violations, while saying that remedial measures have been instituted to correct the infractions.
Dharmala Securities said it had asked for specific instances of the alleged violations before making any reply. Sapphire officials and Cuaycong were not available to comment.
